# THEORYs with `tags` `mathematical-statistics`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds what the Anthology of the SOTA does not: reading whose subject no anthology topic can hold. The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Mathematical statistics** — the theory of statistical inference read for itself — comparison and sufficiency of experiments (Blackwell, Le Cam deficiency), statistical decision theory, the sufficiency theorems (Fisher–Neyman, Basu, Bahadur) and bounds on estimation. Bayesian modelling is probabilistic-modeling (ADR-031).

| [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) | For experiments on a finite parameter set, being at least as informative for every decision problem is the same as being able to simulate the other by a randomisation | Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), Theorem 8 with Theorems 1–3: for experiments with finitely many states and decision problems with bounded losses, α attains every loss vector β attains, in every problem, exactly when a Markov kernel turns α's observation into β's under every state. The direction from simulation to informativeness is Blackwell (1951); the finite converse is Sherman and Stein (1951); the general converse is proved in 1953. It is a qualitative order and says nothing about how much worse an incomparable experiment is. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-157](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-157.md) | The classical theorems on sufficient statistics need only the copy/discard structure of Markov kernels: Basu's theorem holds in every Markov category, and Fisher–Neyman and Bahadur need only strict positivity, not the existence of conditional distributions | Fritz (2020), [LIT-772](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-772.md), read in [NOTE-588](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-588.md), Theorems 14.5, 15.8 and 16.3 with the definitions of Sections 13–15. Sufficiency, completeness and ancillarity are stated with copy, discard, composition and almost-sure equality alone. Basu's theorem follows with no further axiom; Fisher–Neyman and Bahadur use strict positivity, which Stoch has although it lacks regular conditionals. The match with the classical theorems is shown in FinStoch (Fisher–Neyman) and through bounded completeness in Stoch (Basu), not for measure-theoretic Fisher–Neyman. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-161](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-161.md) | In the semantic rate–distortion frameworks of 2021–2025, meaning is a latent variable with a known joint law with the observation, so their limits are indirect source-coding limits; a posterior-matching semantic distortion is, with KL divergence, exactly the information bottleneck, and with total variation a uniform bound on lost decision value | From the readings of Zhao et al. (2025), [LIT-793](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-793.md), Chai et al. (2023), [LIT-812](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-812.md), and the survey of Xin, Fan and Letaief (2024), [LIT-823](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-823.md). These frameworks fix meaning as a hidden S with a known p(S, X); their theorems are indirect rate–distortion results that do not depend on what S is. Zhao et al.'s posterior distortion reduces, for KL, to I(S;X) − I(S;Y), making the function the information bottleneck ([LIT-338](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-338.md)), and for TV bounds the extra Bayes risk of every bounded loss. The two identities are this record's derivations, not the papers'. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-176](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-176.md) | A task-loss stitching penalty compares representations in one decision problem, through a fixed top network and a restricted map class, so it is not Blackwell's order: representations that are functions of each other can stitch differently, and a negative penalty shows the fitted map did not reproduce the layers it replaced | Bansal, Nakkiran & Barak (2021), [LIT-850](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-850.md), define the stitching penalty L_ℓ(r; A) − L(A), with L_ℓ(r; A) the least task loss of A's top layers fed r through a map from a simple family S, and use it to call one representation better than another. Read against Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), and [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md), that ordering is one coordinate of the comparison of experiments with the decision rules cut down to A's head composed with S. It is not invariant under Blackwell equivalence, which the paper intends, and it meets Blackwell's order only where the fitted map reproduces the replaced layers exactly. The relations are this record's derivations from the paper's definitions, not the paper's. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-215](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-215.md) | A Hawkes process with a Lipschitz rate function and signed kernels has a unique stationary regime, which suitably started versions approach, when the Lipschitz-weighted absolute kernel mass is below one (a spectral radius below one, for a network) or when the rate is bounded | Brémaud and Massoulié (1996), [LIT-1035](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1035.md), read in [NOTE-728](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-728.md): Theorems 1, 2, 7 and 8, proved. Inhibition is allowed because the conditions use \|h\|. The conditions are sufficient, not necessary; the kernels are fixed in time; uniqueness is among solutions with finite mean intensity. In the linear excitatory case the condition is the branching ratio below one, but in the nonlinear signed case the spectral-radius quantity is a bound, not a branching ratio, and a bounded rate needs no bound on the kernels at all. Nothing is proved about cascade sizes or about what happens past the threshold. | Active |
| [THEORY-280](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-280.md) | The bisimulation metric between two finite Markov chains can be estimated from sampled transitions without a transition model, to accuracy ε with a number of samples polynomial in the state-space sizes and 1/ε² | Calo, Jonsson, Neu, Schwartz & Segovia-Aguas (2025), [LIT-948](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-948.md), read in [NOTE-763](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-763.md). Bicausal occupancy couplings are characterised by constraints that use only each chain's sampled occupancy measure over consecutive state pairs. A stochastic primal-dual method on them gets an ε-accurate estimate with probability 1−δ from O((\|X\|\|Y\|(\|X\|+\|Y\|) + (\|X\|+\|Y\|)log(1/δ))/((1−γ)²ε²)) independent samples per chain. The states must be observed and enumerable, the cost known, and the samples drawn with restarts. A single running stream and latent states are outside it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-308](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-308.md) | The neural Donsker–Varadhan estimator of mutual information is strongly consistent as an extremum estimator over a compact family of critics, and its uniform deviation from the population bound is controlled by the parameter count, not the data dimension | Belghazi et al. (2018), [LIT-256](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-256.md), §3.3 and App. 8.2.2–8.2.3, read in [NOTE-828](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-828.md). On a compact domain with Lebesgue densities, the supremum of the Donsker–Varadhan bound over some compact network family is within any η of the mutual information, and the empirical supremum converges to the population one almost surely. Uniform deviation ε needs Õ(d log d/ε²) samples for d parameters, under bounded, Lipschitz critics. The guarantee is for the exact empirical maximizer, not for gradient training. The finite-sample estimate is not a bound (Poole et al., [LIT-246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-246.md)), and the proof has two gaps a reading found. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-318](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-318.md) | A bound on the max-information between a dataset and the functions an analyst chooses bounds the probability that an adaptively chosen statistic overfits that dataset, and differential privacy supplies the bound, so a holdout can validate many adaptively chosen statistics | Dwork, Feldman, Hardt, Pitassi, Reingold & Roth (2015), [LIT-964](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-964.md), Supplementary Material only, read in [NOTE-848](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-848.md) (Skimmed: the main text was not reached). Theorem 2 and Lemma 5 are proved there and were checked: P[overfit] ≤ 2^{I∞}·max P[overfit], and ε-DP gives I∞ ≤ log₂e·εn. Thresholdout's guarantee (Theorem 11), n = O(ln(m/β)/τ²·min{B, √(B ln(m/β))/τ}), is stated with its proof elsewhere. Statistical queries on a discrete universe only, and a procedure that prevents inflation, not a correction for a search already run. | Proposed |
